$comment: Reference trajectory for the host routing contract (docs/research/host-routing-contract.md). This is a fixture demonstrating the decision shape at each round. It is NOT a benchmark: it does not claim these decisions are optimal, and nothing here should be read as evidence that they are. Whether they are good is answered by a separate evaluation.
task: fix a failing auth test by tightening token validation

trajectory.observed: trajectory starts; no file reads yet

decision.reason: repository search needs no tool use and no reasoning; strongest available capacity is wasted here
still exploration; context requirement grew but capability requirement did not

trajectory.observed: mutation about to be authored; tools required

decision.reason: first round that benefits from tools and effort together

trajectory.observed: test run failed; identical error on two consecutive runs

decision.reason: two identical failures are capability evidence, not availability evidence; raise effort rather than switching provider

trajectory.$note: Contrast: a 429 here would be availability, and the correct action would be a different healthy route at the SAME capability. Conflating them routes to a stronger model for a reason that was never true.

trajectory.observed: mutation failed to apply; patch rejected twice

decision.reason: repeated semantic failure at high context justifies a capability increase, not a retry
de-escalation: the half of adaptive routing that is usually not demonstrated

$invariants: provider is an output, not an input; the decision omits it where the host does not expose it per-round
a model transition updates model, provider, effort, context ceiling, modality and transport health together
the model that answered is verified against the model requested before anything learns from the round
transport failure and capability failure are distinct; only the second justifies a stronger model
